posts.cooked:
We haven't had a game event in awhile, so here it is. The same rules as the first villain beatdown are in effect, with a couple of additions:

 

*After you create a hero team, you must use the same team against each of their nemses.

*If you win a game, we gain points equal to the villain's difficulty. Simply put your name in the column of the villain.

*If you win an advanced game, you get double the points. Put your name twice in that column.

*Losses still count as 1 point. Put you name in the loss column.

*Advance losses count as 2 points. Put your name twice in the loss column.

*If you can, post a session report here.

*If you don't have a nemesis for a hero, make one up with what you have. You still need to play a number of games equal to the number of heroes on the team.

*You only need to play 1 nemesis game for each hero.

*Iron Legacy only counts as 1 nemesis game. The game can be repeated for a second nemesis, but you still need to play a number of games equal to the number of heroes on the team.

*If a team wins every match against their nemeses, we get a bonus, and you can name your team. You can replay any losses.

 

All game can be submitted here.

 

You will have a full week for this event. The deadline is Monday, January 13, 2014, 11:59 PM CST.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
First game for Omnitron-X/The Wraith/MisterFixer/Expatriette ends in defeat to Advanced Cosmitron.

The game went pretty well, until Fixer pulled Salvage yard, and drunk on power (and Omni wanting his components back) we decided to Singularity then Salvage yard.  12 Damage to Omni was awesome, the Mars Base playing Dust and Omni playing 2 assault Drones and EPE the next turn was not.  Patience was a virtue we lacked this game, and it cost us.

 

Rematch was a victory:  Meteor Storm early let the team get set up, stomping Omni down to 42 HP before he played Singularity, then Mars Base played Red dust, we destroy Red Dust in time for another Singularity, followed of course by Red Dust.

That left Omni dead, Expat and Wraith at half health and Fixer nearly full.  A few turns of Driving mantis and stealth based survival later Omni played 5 drones (fortunately three were repair) and an EPE.

With Wraith ar 3hp, Fixer at 9 and Expat at 6hp things looked hopeless.  Omni let Expat draw a card for his incap and she got unload.  We look at the numbers.  Wraith Barrages for 10, Fixer hits Omni for 3, and Expat hits for 17 (including an assault rifle+incendiary shot at Fixer) to destroy the 28HP Cosmitron.

Fortunately that ended the game, because he had enough fire power to end us on his turn if Omni had his old rule in this version.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
(It didn't end up mattering for me, Pydro, but it occurs to me to ask - after assembling your team, are you allowed to switch versions of the heroes involved between rounds?  Like, could you play normal Legacy, Wraith and Bunker for one game, then Young Legacy and Freedom Six Wraith and Bunker, and then Rook City Wraith and the WW2 heroes?  Or must you play the same version of each hero all the way through?)

Played the first of my three matches - Wraith, Tachyon and Ra vs. their nemeses, in the opposite of that order.  One of my earliest matches featured these three heroes (in the other order), and has always stuck in my mind, so after confirming that this would be a worthwhile choice, I decided this would be my team.  I'm starting off with the Ennead fight, as they're among my favorite villains and I have fought them only three times before.  And fittingly enough, the battle is Ra and two women, one "bright" and the other  "dark", vs. the Ennead's resident sun god Atum and his two ladyfriends, Isis and Nephthys, the goddesses of Birth and Death.  Even the HP totals are close, with the Ennead having one more HP among them than the heroes - Atum and Ra at 30, Isis and Wraith at 26, Tacky at 27 and Neph at 28.  For setting, I decided to go with Rook City, not because I especially wanted the extra difficulty but simply because I was due to revisit it, and figured it would worsen the battle less against the Ennead than it would against either Matriarch or GloomSpite.

So, the battle started off with an Elemental Storm, burning each hero for 3, with Isis zapping Ra for 2 and Nephtys throwing an extra fire damage at everyone.  That put the hero team down 14 HP with one card, but Throwing Knives and Accelerated Assault retaliated for 6 (Tachy chaining through HUD Goggles and reluctantly dumping a Synaptic), then Ra summoned his Staff to heal 3 and threw it at Isis for 4, just to teach her a lesson (and also because he had another Summon Staff in hand).  Rook City started off annoying with a Scum and Villainy, which played Sun's Fury for 1 damage to each hero, with no triggers.  The Desert's Wrath then destroyed S&V, dealing 2 more damage to all heroes (counting Nephtys) and an extra 2 to Tachyon, but preventing the 2 that S&V was set to deal at the end of round 2.  Wraith put down a Stun Bolt, but didn't use it just yet, because Tachy had Hypersonic Assault; after Ra re-summoned his staff, he roasted Isis down to 15, while being only down 3 himself.  An Ambitious Racketeer stuck his nose into things, which strikes me as less than wise of him; since it doesn't specify which hero targets it attacks, I assume I get to choose, so I had him shoot at Ra and Wraith, leaving Tachy more able to keep Pushing the Limits.  More Desert Wrath happened, disposing of the Idiot Racketeer but unable to deal any damage; Wraith put down Smoke Bombs before Throwing more Knives, Tachy kept up the Hypersonic pressure and threw an extremely premature Lightspeed Barrage for just 5 damage, before using Research Grant to refill her hand to the same 3 cards she was allowed to play (those numbers becoming 2 without PtL).  Ra put down an Inferno, leaving Isis at 2, then a Falling Statue started to fall onto Tachyon's head, but got confused by the smoke and instead hit Ra (for the full 3 since it's irreducible).  That was the only thing the Smoke Bombs would ever accomplish before Mass Overheating got them (you'd think that would just make them smoke harder, but whatevs), and Wraith also threw out her Knives since she was about to lose her third target, and it gave her an excuse to switch to Stun Bolts now that Hypersonics were done.  She gave Nephthys a Throat Jab before Stunning Atum, then Tachy played a Quick Insight, discarded two Nimble Strikes, Sucker Punched Isis to death (revealing an incap ability which can be summarized as "Oooh, Tachy like!"), and threw a much more impressive Lightspeed Barrage at Atum for 10 damage, ensuring that Nephthys would become the highest-HP Ennie - this matters because Atum frequently plays extra Sun's Wraths or Mass Overheatings, both of which have the highest-HP Ennie dealing their damage, so they wouldn't work this next turn due to Throat Jab.  Lacking anything better to do, Ra played Blazing Tornado so he could fry Atum for 4 instead of 3.  Another Scum and Villainy chose a reasonably good time to happen, playing The Grave Beckons...in itself, this did nothing, but it triggered Ankh abilities for the first time, so Neph healed herself and Atum for 1, and Atum played a Sun card, which was another Mass Overheating, and this time Tachy and Ra disposed of their solitary Equipments so that Wraith could keep Stun Bolt, even though she had a spare in hand.  About this time I realized I had completely forgotten to apply Nemesis bonuses in either direction, so I figured I'd see whether I could manage to recalculate from the top:

Round 1:  Elemental Storm [W-23, T-24, R-24], Isis (instead hitting T who falls to 22), Nephthys [W-22, T-21, R-22]...the team is actually down 18 HP with one card.  Throwing Knives [I-25, A-29, N-27], Accelerated Assault [I-24, A-28, N-26], Staff of Ra played for healing and thrown at Isis for net 5 damage [R-25, I-19].  Scum and Villainy plays Sun's Fury [W-21, T-20, R-23].

Round 2:  The Desert's Wrath [W-20, T-19, R-21], Isis (now hitting Wraith who falls to 18), Nephthys [W-17, T-18, R-19].  Throwing Knives [I-18, A-27, N-25], Hypersonic Assault [I-17, A-26, N-24], Staff of Ra played for healing and Isis Pyred for net 4 [R-22, I-13] - he's 5 lower than I thought, and Isis is only 2 lower.  Ambitious Racketeer still doesn't shoot Tachy [W-15, R-20].

Round 3:  Throwing Knives [I-12, A-25, N-23], Tachy Pushes the Limits and falls to 16, Hypersonic Assault [I-11, A-24, N-22], Lightspeed Barrages Isis down to 6, then Ra plays Inferno with Isis as the primary target, leaving her at 1 [A-21, N-19].  Falling Statue now initially plans to hit on Wraith, but still mistakes Ra for a woman through the smoke, leaving him at 17.

Round 4:  Throat Jab Nephthys to leave her at 17, then Stun Bolt on Atum who ends up at 20.  Tachy PtLs to 14.  I can't see how Isis could be only 1 HP lower now than before when Ra hit her twice with nemesis, but I'll assume it somehow worked so that Tachy still played Sucker Punch to kill her (else she'd have had to discard Sucker Punch and play Nimble Strike on one of the two survivors, and she'd be up a card).  Lightspeed Barrage cuts Atum in half, then Ra burns off half of that, leaving him at 5.  Scum and Villainy plays The Grave Beckons which triggers Nepthys's healing [A-6, N-18].

Okay, so I calculate Atum as having lost 4 more HP than before, and 2 for Nephthys, while shuffling things around for the heroes leaves Ra down 5, Wraith down 2, and Tachy unchanged.  Resuming normal play with the start of round 5, Ancient Magicks destroys PtL and Blazing Tornado, then Atum zaps Wraith and Tachy for 1 each [W-14, T-13]; Nepthys responds by coughing and wheezing and rubbing her bruised throat, which feels okay a moment later ("as your doctor, I advise you not to breathe fire this turn").  Wraith Impromptu-Invents a Utility Belt, plays her second Stun Bolt, and reduces Neph to 16 HP while double-Stunning her.  Tachy has drawn her third Lightspeed Barrage but doesn't want to play it until the last minute, so she uses Quick Insight to put out a pair of Synaptics.  Finally an Enviro card has remained in play past the end of the villain turn, so Ra considers playing Scorched Earth for net 2 damage to each of the two surviving Ennies, but I really want to kill Atum, so I use Inferno for net 4 to him and 2 to Neph (leaving her at 14), then overkills him with Pyre.  I notice that I forgot to do Isis's incap ability, so I belatedly take care of it now; Scum & Villainy self-destructs and causes Neph to deal 2-2 damage to each hero, with a net effect of 1 damage to Ra (leaving him at 16)...I forget how you pick which villain is supposed to deal the damage on S&V, but of course in this case it doens't matter.  Then a Statue falls, and Neph is tied with Wraith for second-highest HP, so she takes the hit and is left at 11.  Round 6 begins and I do it right this time; dead Isis mills an Impromptu Invention and Ra's other two Summon Staffs, then dead Atum reloads the villain deck with those lovely, harmless Desert Wraths while making it less likely that a Taste of Immortality or Rise to Power will prolong the game.  Sun's Fury is the play, and again all Neph can do is hit Ra for 1.  Wraith plunks down a Micro Targeting Computer to double-stun Neph down to 5, and then Tachy turns her into a grease spot on the pavement with exactly three times as much damage as required.  So much for the Power of the Ennead.

That was awesome, if a bit error-laden (as is typical for me; at least this time, the most consequential error was possible to correct, so the only real glitch was the remote possibility that Isis could have milled all of Wraith's Utility Belts or MCTs if I had done it right).  I'll be moving on shortly to the next match, though I don't know if I want to do all three of them today.

himself.  An Ambitious Racketeer stuck his nose into things, which strikes me as less than wise of him; since it doesn't specify which hero targets it attacks, I assume I get to choose, so I had him shoot at Ra and Wraith, leaving Tachy more able to keep Pushing the Limits.  More Desert Wrath happened, disposing of the Idiot Racketeer but unable to deal any damage; Wraith put down Smoke Bombs before Throwing more Knives, Tachy kept up the Hypersonic pressure and threw an extremely premature Lightspeed Barrage for just 5 damage, before using Research Grant to refill her hand to the same 3 cards she was allowed to play (those numbers becoming 2 without PtL).  Ra put down an Inferno, leaving Isis at 2, then a Falling Statue started to fall onto Tachyon's head, but got confused by the smoke and instead hit Ra (for the full 3 since it's irreducible).  That was the only thing the Smoke Bombs would ever accomplish before Mass Overheating got them (you'd think that would just make them smoke harder, but whatevs), and Wraith also threw out her Knives since she was about to lose her third target, and it gave her an excuse to switch to Stun Bolts now that Hypersonics were done.  She gave Nephthys a Throat Jab before Stunning Atum, then Tachy played a Quick Insight, discarded two Nimble Strikes, Sucker Punched Isis to death (revealing an incap ability which can be summarized as "Oooh, Tachy like!"), and threw a much more impressive Lightspeed Barrage at Atum for 10 damage, ensuring that Nephthys would become the highest-HP Ennie - this matters because Atum frequently plays extra Sun's Wraths or Mass Overheatings, both of which have the highest-HP Ennie dealing their damage, so they wouldn't work this next turn due to Throat Jab.  Lacking anything better to do, Ra played Blazing Tornado so he could fry Atum for 4 instead of 3.  Another Scum and Villainy chose a reasonably good time to happen, playing The Grave Beckons...in itself, this did nothing, but it triggered Ankh abilities for the first time, so Neph healed herself and Atum for 1, and Atum played a Sun card, which was another Mass Overheating, and this time Tachy and Ra disposed of their solitary Equipments so that Wraith could keep Stun Bolt, even though she had a spare in hand.  About this time I realized I had completely forgotten to apply Nemesis bonuses in either direction, so I figured I'd see whether I could manage to recalculate from the top:

Round 1:  Elemental Storm [W-23, T-24, R-24], Isis (instead hitting T who falls to 22), Nephthys [W-22, T-21, R-22]...the team is actually down 18 HP with one card.  Throwing Knives [I-25, A-29, N-27], Accelerated Assault [I-24, A-28, N-26], Staff of Ra played for healing and thrown at Isis for net 5 damage [R-25, I-19].  Scum and Villainy plays Sun's Fury [W-21, T-20, R-23].

Round 2:  The Desert's Wrath [W-20, T-19, R-21], Isis (now hitting Wraith who falls to 18), Nephthys [W-17, T-18, R-19].  Throwing Knives [I-18, A-27, N-25], Hypersonic Assault [I-17, A-26, N-24], Staff of Ra played for healing and Isis Pyred for net 4 [R-22, I-13] - he's 5 lower than I thought, and Isis is only 2 lower.  Ambitious Racketeer still doesn't shoot Tachy [W-15, R-20].

Round 3:  Throwing Knives [I-12, A-25, N-23], Tachy Pushes the Limits and falls to 16, Hypersonic Assault [I-11, A-24, N-22], Lightspeed Barrages Isis down to 6, then Ra plays Inferno with Isis as the primary target, leaving her at 1 [A-21, N-19].  Falling Statue now initially plans to hit on Wraith, but still mistakes Ra for a woman through the smoke, leaving him at 17.

Round 4:  Throat Jab Nephthys to leave her at 17, then Stun Bolt on Atum who ends up at 20.  Tachy PtLs to 14.  I can't see how Isis could be only 1 HP lower now than before when Ra hit her twice with nemesis, but I'll assume it somehow worked so that Tachy still played Sucker Punch to kill her (else she'd have had to discard Sucker Punch and play Nimble Strike on one of the two survivors, and she'd be up a card).  Lightspeed Barrage cuts Atum in half, then Ra burns off half of that, leaving him at 5.  Scum and Villainy plays The Grave Beckons which triggers Nepthys's healing [A-6, N-18].

Okay, so I calculate Atum as having lost 4 more HP than before, and 2 for Nephthys, while shuffling things around for the heroes leaves Ra down 5, Wraith down 2, and Tachy unchanged.  Resuming normal play with the start of round 5, Ancient Magicks destroys PtL and Blazing Tornado, then Atum zaps Wraith and Tachy for 1 each [W-14, T-13]; Nepthys responds by coughing and wheezing and rubbing her bruised throat, which feels okay a moment later ("as your doctor, I advise you not to breathe fire this turn").  Wraith Impromptu-Invents a Utility Belt, plays her second Stun Bolt, and reduces Neph to 16 HP while double-Stunning her.  Tachy has drawn her third Lightspeed Barrage but doesn't want to play it until the last minute, so she uses Quick Insight to put out a pair of Synaptics.  Finally an Enviro card has remained in play past the end of the villain turn, so Ra considers playing Scorched Earth for net 2 damage to each of the two surviving Ennies, but I really want to kill Atum, so I use Inferno for net 4 to him and 2 to Neph (leaving her at 14), then overkills him with Pyre.  I notice that I forgot to do Isis's incap ability, so I belatedly take care of it now; Scum & Villainy self-destructs and causes Neph to deal 2-2 damage to each hero, with a net effect of 1 damage to Ra (leaving him at 16)...I forget how you pick which villain is supposed to deal the damage on S&V, but of course in this case it doens't matter.  Then a Statue falls, and Neph is tied with Wraith for second-highest HP, so she takes the hit and is left at 11.  Round 6 begins and I do it right this time; dead Isis mills an Impromptu Invention and Ra's other two Summon Staffs, then dead Atum reloads the villain deck with those lovely, harmless Desert Wraths while making it less likely that a Taste of Immortality or Rise to Power will prolong the game.  Sun's Fury is the play, and again all Neph can do is hit Ra for 1.  Wraith plunks down a Micro Targeting Computer to double-stun Neph down to 5, and then Tachy turns her into a grease spot on the pavement with exactly three times as much damage as required.  So much for the Power of the Ennead.

That was awesome, if a bit error-laden (as is typical for me; at least this time, the most consequential error was possible to correct, so the only real glitch was the remote possibility that Isis could have milled all of Wraith's Utility Belts or MCTs if I had done it right).  I'll be moving on shortly to the next match, though I don't know if I want to do all three of them today.

title: SotM Event #8 - Villain Beatdown Nemesis Edition!!!
